glossary.meaning: Utmost good faith: the insured must disclose every material fact before cover is granted.
A lawful financial interest. You are worse off if the insured event happens.
Pays the actual ascertained loss (health, property, motor).
Pays a pre-fixed sum on the event (life, critical illness, hospital cash).
The insurer steps into the insured's shoes to recover from the at-fault third party after paying the claim.
Proportionate sharing of an indemnity claim among insurers covering the same risk.
A fixed percentage of each admissible claim borne by the insured.
The first slice of a claim borne by the insured before the insurer pays.
Parent, spouse or child nominee under s.39(7) of the Insurance Act who owns the proceeds rather than holding them for the heirs.
PV of the future income a person would have provided to dependants.
Health cover that pays once the aggregate claims in a year exceed the threshold.
Retirement income targeted as a % of pre-retirement income.
The maximum first-year withdrawal (% of the starting corpus, then inflated each year) that survives with at least 95% probability.
The damage done by poor returns early in the withdrawal phase, even when average returns are unchanged.
A stream of payments for life or a fixed period, bought from an insurer. Deferred = starts after 12+ months. Immediate = within 12 months.
The IT Act 2025 concept replacing previous year and assessment year, e.g. 1 Apr 2026 to 31 Mar 2027.
Resident but Not Ordinarily Resident: taxed on Indian income plus foreign income from a business controlled or profession set up in India.
Protects gains accrued up to 31 Jan 2018 on STT-paid equity by using the FMV on that date as cost.
A fund with ≥65% in debt or money-market instruments, acquired on or after 1 Apr 2023. Gains are always short-term.
Buying just before a bonus record date and selling the originals at a loss. That loss is disallowed and added to the bonus units' cost.
Income taxed in the investors' hands instead of the vehicle's (REIT rent, Category I/II AIF non-business income).
Dying without a valid Will for some or all property.
Agnate: related wholly through males. Cognate: related but not wholly through males.
An instrument explaining, altering or adding to a Will, executed like a Will.
A copy of the Will certified under the court's seal, granted only to the executor.
A court grant when there is no executor or the executor cannot or will not act.
Authorises collection of specified debts and securities of a deceased person. It does not confer title.
A trust where the trustees decide the beneficiaries' shares. Taxed at the maximum marginal rate.
Changing the name in revenue records for fiscal purposes. It is not proof of title.
Decision-making that 'satisfices' within limits of time, information and ability (Herbert Simon).
Kahneman–Tversky (1979): outcomes judged against a reference point, with losses weighing more than gains.
Treating money as non-fungible depending on its source or intended use (Thaler).
How consistently an investor sticks to stated risk preferences under real market stress.
A long-term, goal-based mix rebalanced periodically, not changed on market views.

quickRevision: Pattern: 90 × 1 + 6 cases × 5 × 2 = 150 marks, 3 hours, pass 60%, −25% for each wrong answer. Excel or Calc is available.
Contribution and subrogation apply only to indemnity policies. Defined-benefit policies all pay.
Apply the deductible first, then the co-pay: (Claim − Deductible) × (1 − co-pay).
Section 45: a life policy is incontestable after 3 years. Health: no contest after a 5-year moratorium except fraud.
Beneficial nominee (parent, spouse, child) owns life-insurance money. Other nominees are trustees for the heirs.
MWPA policy: wife and/or children only, cannot be changed, survives divorce, safe from creditors.
HLV ≥ needs-based cover. A higher income growth rate raises HLV.
Top-up threshold is per claim, super top-up threshold is aggregate.
Car NCB of up to 50% follows the owner, not the car. Third-party motor cover is compulsory.
EPF employer 12% = 3.67% EPF + 8.33% EPS + 0.5% EDLI + 0.5% admin. Withdrawal is tax-free after 5 years' continuous service.
Gratuity = 15 × wage × years ÷ 26. Tax-free up to ₹20 lakh.
PPF: ₹500–₹1.5 lakh, 15 years, loan from FY 3 to FY 6 at 25%, partial withdrawal after 5 FYs, extensions in 5-year blocks.
NPS at 60: at least 20% annuity (40% for government). ≤₹8 lakh can be taken in full. 60% lump sum is tax-free. Premature exit needs 80% annuity.
NPS partial withdrawal: after 3 years, 25% of own contribution, up to 4 times before 60.
UPS: 50% of the average basic after 25 years, ₹10,000 minimum after 10 years, family payout 60%.
Annuity without return of purchase price pays the most, with return of purchase price the least.
SCSS ₹30 lakh, POMIS ₹9 lakh / ₹15 lakh, reverse mortgage up to 20 years with receipts tax-free.
SWR is a first-year % that rises with inflation regardless of market falls. India ≈ 3–3.5%. 10–30% equity gives the highest SWR.
Corpus = annual need ÷ SWR. A longer horizon gives a lower SWR and a bigger corpus.
New regime: nil to ₹4 lakh, then 5% steps, 30% above ₹24 lakh. Rebate up to ₹60,000 if income ≤ ₹12 lakh.
NOR: non-resident 9 of 10 years OR ≤729 days in 7 years. A deemed resident is always RNOR.
LTCL only against LTCG. STCL against any capital gain. 8-year carry forward. Speculative loss 4 years.
LTCG 12.5% everywhere. STT equity: STCG 20%, LTCG above ₹1.25 lakh. Surcharge on capital gains is capped at 15%.
Always short-term: MLDs, debt MFs bought on or after 1-4-2023, unlisted bonds or debentures, depreciable assets.
Indexation survives only for land or buildings bought before 23-7-2024 (lower of 20% indexed or 12.5%).
Grandfathering: cost = max(actual, min(FMV on 31-1-2018, sale price)).
No deductions from dividends from Tax Year 2026-27. Buyback is now taxed as capital gains.
Non-relative gifts above ₹50,000 in aggregate are fully taxable. Nephews, nieces and cousins are NOT relatives.
ESOP: perquisite uses FMV on exercise. Holding period starts at allotment.
SGB redemption is tax-free only for an original subscriber held to maturity.
REIT rent passes through to unit-holders. InvIT rent is taxed at the trust. AIF Cat III has no pass-through.
Hindu intestacy: Class I heirs take together. The father is Class II. Uterine siblings are excluded.
Muslim: widow 1/4 or 1/8, Will limited to 1/3, no birth-right, an oral Will is valid.
Will registration is optional, needs no stamp duty, and can be revoked any time. Marriage does not revoke a Hindu Will.
Probate goes only to the executor. s.213 compulsory probate was omitted in 2025.
SEBI allows up to 3 nominees (from 1 Sep 2026). Banks allow up to 4.
Discretionary trust is taxed at MMR (42.744%). A revocable trust is taxed in the settlor's hands.
Emotional biases: loss aversion, overconfidence, endowment, status quo, regret. Cognitive: mental accounting, framing, anchoring.
SEBI IA Regulation 16: objective risk profile, communicated and consented to BEFORE advice, including free trials.

examStrategy: Time split: about 70 minutes for the 90 MCQs (45 seconds each), about 90 minutes for the 6 cases (15 minutes each), and 20 minutes for review and Excel checks.
Do the MCQs first for quick marks, but don't let them eat into case time: the cases carry 40% of the marks.
In each case, read all 5 sub-questions first, set the zero date, decide type 0 or 1, and build one Excel table you can reuse.
Negative marking: −0.25 per wrong MCQ and −0.5 per wrong case answer. Answer when you can eliminate two options, and skip pure guesses.
Use the real rate (1+r)/(1+i) − 1 for every inflation-linked PV, and round as the question implies (the workbook uses 2 decimals).
Module 12 (45 marks) plus retirement (30) and insurance (25) make up two-thirds of the paper, so master them first.
For tax questions, identify the asset and holding period first, then the rate. Watch for the 2026 changes (dividend deductions, buyback, SGB, Tax Year).
For estate questions, list the surviving heirs, keep only the highest class present, and count shares.
In risk-profiling scenarios, prefer the answer that revises the goal or reduces risk when need exceeds capacity, and choose disciplined, rules-based adviser actions.
